title: Untrusted data-file strings reach the terminal unsanitized (terminal escape injection via warning/debug output)
description: Resource names from RESOURCE.001 bytecode (TTM 0xF01F/0xF02F text operands, ADS RES-chunk TTM names) and SCRANTIC.SCR (ads_names, debug mode) are decoded with String::from_utf8_lossy, which keeps C0 control bytes such as ESC and BEL. When the named resource is missing, the AssetError text embedding the name verbatim and without a length cap is written to stderr by eprintln! in normal runs. A supplier of modified data files can make the desktop binary, run from a terminal as the README instructs, emit arbitrary terminal control sequences (screen clear/spoof, title set, OSC 52 clipboard write where allowed) and very large lines.
root_cause: Data-file strings are treated as display-safe: from_utf8_lossy without control filtering (resource.rs:209, resource.rs:129), AssetError::Missing(name.to_string()) (resource.rs:40), printed via eprintln!("warning: {e}") (ttm.rs:278, ttm.rs:290, engine/mod.rs:459) without escaping or truncation.
intended_behavior: Data-file text is shown only after control/non-printable characters are escaped and length is capped, so the files affect only the program's own rendering.

trace.description: RESOURCE.001 read whole from the install directory.
0xF01F/0xF02F text operand becomes op.text via from_utf8_lossy (keeps ESC/BEL, unbounded length).
Script name passed to archive.scr(name); missing name yields error.
AssetError::Missing(name.to_string()) embeds the raw name; Display prints it verbatim.
eprintln!("warning: {e}") writes raw control bytes to stderr (also ttm.rs:290, engine/mod.rs:459).

evidence.description: No control-character filter or length limit on op.text.
ADS RES TTM names decoded the same way; reach engine/mod.rs:459.
Unconditional eprintln of the data-controlled name.
Debug-mode eprintln of scene_name() including ads_names from SCRANTIC.SCR.

conditions.description: Data files altered so a TTM/ADS resource name contains control sequences and names a missing resource.
Desktop binary stderr attached to a terminal (the .scr build has no console); effect depends on the terminal emulator.
User starts the binary from a shell as README/AGENTS.md instruct.

execution.attacker_perspective: Supplier of modified RESOURCE.001 bytes; no other access.
payloads: X.TTM: PAG: [01 00]; TT3: RLE literal [1F F0] + b"\x1b]0;PWNED-TITLE\x07\x1b]52;c;aWQK\x07\x1b[2J" + [00]
Same opcode with a 1 MiB name of 'A' bytes
instructions: Build t.rs against the harness rlib (unchanged src/assets and src/engine/ttm.rs) inside sandbox-run.sh with -C opt-level=3 -C overflow-checks=off -C panic=abort.
Synthesize RESOURCE.MAP/.001 holding X.TTM, call Archive::new, archive.ttm("X.TTM") and run_frame for scene 0, stderr to a scratch file.
execution.observed_result: stderr: 'warning: missing screensaver file: ' followed by raw 033 ] 0 ; PWNED-TITLE \a 033 ] 5 2 ; c ; a W Q K \a 033 [ 2 J \n. The 1 MiB name produced a single 1,048,612-byte write. Exit 0.

remediation.strategy: Escape and length-cap data-derived names before printing (or sanitize at parse time); add a regression test that an error built from a name containing \x1b contains no raw 0x1b.

likelihood.reason: Requires tampered data files and running the desktop binary from a terminal.

impact.reason: Terminal integrity only: output spoofing/clearing, title changes, OSC 52 clipboard writes where permitted; no code execution in the program.

confidence.reason: Raw control bytes on stderr observed through unchanged code; only the terminal-side effect depends on the emulator.
